d5288620dd988e5e: KUALA LUMPUR: Less than a year after its debut on Bursa Malaysia, ISF Group Bhd is looking to further diversify its revenue base with recurring income sources from partnerships with states water authority to reduce non-revenue water (NRW).

While the company has built its recent growth momentum by riding the data centre boom across Malaysia, its management is cultivating its next major growth drive through cutting-edge technology partnerships to deliver comprehensive NRW solutions.

"ISF is looking at elevating our position to public infra, like projects from PAAB (Perbadanan Aset Air Bhd), and projects from state governments," said its group managing director Jeff Ai Boon Chen in an exclusive interview with Business Times.

To execute this vision, the company is finalising a strategic joint venture with a Hong Kong-listed subsidiary of a major Chinese water firm to introduce smart meters and AI-driven monitoring software to local state water authorities.

"So, instead of working conventionally, like we just purchase technology from them, we will be working as joint venture partners, in which each company will own a stake in this subsidiary. Because we are looking at the long term, rather than every time we need one-off technology," said Ai.

He added that in China, the water supply authority can control the flow of water in each house, through digital sensors and valves in the smart meters, to ensure commercial NRWs - customers not paying their water bills - are addressed there.

ISF's competitive edge lies in acting as the local executor and coordinator, filling the gap where foreign technology suppliers struggle with local deployment and state authorities lack full operational capability.

"So, the technology, the manufacturing and everything will be handled by them. So, there won't be any conflict of interest. So, that is why we work as partners... But, with this joint venture, ISF will act as a so-called party to coordinate everything.
"We execute the work, pipe replacement, everything we can do ourselves," said Ai.
ISF is already in negotiations with a state government in the northern peninsular to implement the NRW management system.
The company is currently funding a proof of concept (POC) to demonstrate the efficacy of this system, paving the way for long-term recurring revenue models, he said.

The commercial arrangements that ISF is looking at with the state's water authority is either through profit sharing or one-off project costs that come with operation and maintenance (O&M) contracts, said Ai.

"But it is a long-term thing that we are looking at because we need to have recurrent income rather than purely doing projects. What we are doing now is actually preparing for the next wave (to ride on).
"Hopefully, by maybe the third or fourth quarter of 2027, there will be concrete things. So, the next growth story will begin," he said.
Riding the data centre wave while maintaining strategic diversification
While NRW technology represents the future horizon, data centre (DC) projects serve as ISF's immediate revenue engine.
The company's involvement in the sector dates back nearly a decade, giving it an early-mover advantage over competitors.

Riding on the DC construction wave, ISF's net profits in the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY25) surged 163 per cent to RM25.34 million, compared with RM9.64 million in the preceding financial year.
In the first six months of the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY26), ISF reported net profits of RM12.5 million, on the back of RM57.6 million in revenue.
The six-month revenue was 58.4 per cent of FY25's total, and already exceeded FY24's revenue of RM54.67 million.
DC works have grown substantially as a share of overall revenue, but management remains steadfast in diversifying across multiple asset classes to protect the business against cyclical shifts.

"So, over the years, it has increased from maybe 10 to 15 percent to I think exceeding 50 percent revenue for FY25. So, we are still looking at revenue from DC jobs also exceeding 50 percent for FY26," said Ai.
However, DC plumbing and piping is only one of the capabilities that ISF could do.
The group is also involved in industrial and commercial assets piping contracts, as well as water distribution and sewerage.
"We consistently tell the public that we are a diversified plumbing contractor. So, every cycle is a good cycle for ISF because you know, we do everything. We are not telling you we can only do DC.

"We still maintain 15 per cent for residential, commercial, industrial and other stuff. So, maybe next year, when the market share of DCs eventually gets smaller, maybe slowly to 30 per cent, our other segments will slightly increase to between 30 and 40 per cent (of revenue)," said Ai.
Looking ahead, ISF anticipates a temporary stabilisation in DC tendering as the industry pivots to execution, opening up space for healthcare and medical infrastructure projects.

"I foresee there will be a bit of a slowdown of the DC standards starting from the first or second quarter of next year. Now is the awarding period, a lot of announcements. So, next year will be the so-called execution year."

"I am looking at next year, maybe we will shift more on the industrial and also on the hospitals, healthcare kind of things. At the end of next year, there will be quite a number of hospitals to be built," said AI.
Institutional Backing Through IPO

ISF's shift from a private entity to a publicly listed company was guided by a desire to install strong corporate governance and attract top professional talent rather than maintaining a strict family dynasty, said AI.

"So, in order for good talent to get into the business, of course, we need to be transparent. Since day one, we are not looking at turning ISF into a family legacy. I've never had the mindset that I'm going to pass ISF down to my children.
"Because my initial intention is very simple. I look at other companies, let's say Hilton. We don't even know who the boss is, but everything is operating smoothly," said Ai.
This institutional transparency brought by being a publicly-listed company has attracted major fund managers, collectively holding more than 20 per cent of ISF's share base.

Despite interest from existing institutional investors to increase their stakes, ISF is adequately capitalised with existing proceeds from its initial public offering (IPO) and internally generated cash to fund its robust tender pipeline.
"Currently, we still have some cash reserves from the IPO. So far, we are still okay with using our existing cash to support our growth," said Ai.

According to its 2025 annual report, institutional investors of ISF include Kumpulan Sentiasa Cemerlang Sdn Bhd, Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd, Hong Leong Dana Makmur, KAF Tactical Fund and AIA Public Takaful Bhd.
However, none of the institutions are substantial shareholders of ISF.
ISF raised RM61.15 million from its IPO in January, with nearly two-third of the proceeds reserved for purchasing operational materials and paying subcontractors.

About 19 per cent is allocated to establish and expand operational facilities, including a new head office at its home base in Johor, and new regional offices in Selangor or Negri Sembilan, and Penang.
A portion of the capital raised is further allocated toward expanding its fleet of heavy machinery and recruiting additional personnel.
Funds from the IPO proceeds and its internally-generated cash are currently enough for its current tender book balance of approximately RM600 million, said Ai.
Historically, ISF managed to secure between 20 and 30 per cent of its tender book as orders.
"So, we are still looking at an annual replenishment of RM150 million per year for new wins," he said.
Defending Profit Margins

ISF commands strong profit margins by maintaining direct operational control, capturing economies of scale, and reducing dependency on third-party subcontractors. As of 6M FY26, ISF's gross margin stood at 30.89 per cent.
The group is looking at improving its gross margins over the next two years, said Ai.

"So, actually, why we are able to command good margins is because of the economy of scale. We are one of the largest plumbing contractors, so we are able to have a better command on the pricing with the suppliers.
"Secondly, we do a lot of things in-house," he said.

To tackle localised labour constraints particularly in Johor where labor competition with Singapore is intense, ISF utilises independent subcontractors strictly for supplemental labour while retaining full ownership of equipment and management.
ISF remains unthreatened by foreign entrants or Chinese investments, as those entities typically operate in closed, in-house ecosystems that fall outside its core target client base.
While the group has been registering strong profit growth, ISF has not declared a dividend, as it prioritises reinvesting earnings into expansions.
The group does not have a dividend policy at the moment.
"We do not have a formal policy on issuing dividends, because, as you can see, our growth is exponential. So, we need to conserve quite substantial cash with us to support our projects," said Ai.
As of Oct 15, ISF's share price appreciated more than 65 per cent to 80 sen apiece, valuing the group at RM795 million.

75fcd5b6d2245a88: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's third-quarter 2026 advance gross domestic product (GDP) estimate of 5.3 per cent is a positive surprise despite external shocks, particularly the ongoing US-Iran conflict, economists said.
They told Business Times that while growth moderated from six per cent in the preceding quarter, the slowdown did not necessarily signal a broad-based loss of economic momentum.

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said proactive government measures, including targeted fuel subsidies through MyKad introduced last year, had helped cushion the economy against external shocks.
Petroliam Nasional Bhd's efforts to secure fuel supplies from outside the Strait of Hormuz also helped minimise disruptions to domestic economic activity, he added.

Foreign investor interest in Malaysia and stronger demand for technology-related sectors had also supported growth, while full employment and relatively contained inflation helped sustain consumer spending.

"Overall, it is a positive surprise and it looks like the growth numbers could be surprised on the upside with the prevailing GDP growth projection currently standing between 4.8 per cent to 5.3 per cent," the economist said.
He added that growth of 5.3 per cent would put Malaysia's economy above its estimated trend growth rate of around 4.7 per cent.

According to the advance estimate released by the Statistics Department today, Malaysia's GDP is estimated to have grown 5.3 per cent in Q3, slightly higher than the 5.2 per cent recorded in the corresponding period last year.
Bank Negara Malaysia is scheduled to release the official Q3 GDP figures on Nov 18.
Growth eased from six per cent in the preceding quarter, with all economic sectors expanding except mining and quarrying.
For the first nine months of 2026, the economy grew 5.5 per cent, compared with 4.8 per cent in the same period last year.
The services sector remained the main growth driver, expanding 5.4 per cent, supported by wholesale and retail trade, information and communication, as well as finance and insurance activities.

Manufacturing growth accelerated to 7.5 per cent from 7.3 per cent in the preceding quarter, driven by export-oriented industries, particularly electrical, electronic and optical products, as well as petroleum, chemicals, rubber and plastics products.
Construction growth eased to six per cent from 6.5 per cent, supported by non-residential projects, particularly data centres, and specialised construction works.
The agriculture sector rebounded 1.3 per cent after contracting 3.7 per cent in the preceding quarter, driven by oil palm and livestock activities.
In contrast, mining and quarrying contracted 4.9 per cent, reversing the 9.2 per cent expansion recorded in the second quarter, following a decline in crude oil and condensate production.

Despite the expansion, Universiti Teknologi Mara senior lecturer Dr Mohamad Idham Md Razak said Malaysia should remain mindful of risks stemming from its exposure to global trade and the current AI investment cycle.
He said softer global technology spending could weigh on semiconductor exports, manufacturing activity and data centre investments.
Higher oil prices could raise businesses' operating costs and further erode household purchasing power.
"Another concern is whether domestic consumption can remain strong if wages fail to keep pace with living costs.

"Malaysia should therefore strengthen domestic economic resilience by improving productivity, supporting small and medium enterprises, attracting higher-value investments and developing new export markets.

"The priority is not simply to maintain headline growth, but to ensure that growth is broad-based and sustainable, so the economy can withstand external shocks without placing excessive pressure on households or public finances," Idham said.

He said Malaysia remains on a relatively solid growth trajectory, but sustaining this momentum will depend on domestic demand, the quality of investments and efforts to diversify the economy's growth drivers.

eebc18f760f012f3: PUCHONG: An ordinary chair bought from IKEA has become part of contractor Kong Hean Fui’s daily struggle to protect his 15-year-old son from hurting himself.

He has adapted it with makeshift straps to help keep Kong Wei Yang safe when involuntary movements take hold of his body. The force can be so intense that the restraints repeatedly need repairing or replacing.
Yet the chair cannot always protect him.

When Wei Yang’s spasms strike without warning, he may slam his feet against the floor or bite his fingers so hard that his parents struggle to free them without causing further injury. Sometimes, both must step in to restrain him.
For Kong and his wife, Wong Yin Teng, caring for their son means staying alert to danger throughout the day and night.
Wei Yang has Lesch-Nyhan syndrome, a rare genetic disorder that causes neurological impairment, involuntary muscle movements and compulsive self-injury.
Now, his biting has become harder to control despite medication. His parents hope he can finally undergo a procedure doctors have recommended for years, but they cannot afford it.

An appeal featured by FMT in July raised about RM40,000 before donations slowed. The family now needs between RM280,000 and RM300,000 for deep brain stimulation (DBS), a procedure intended to help control his symptoms.
The money collected remains with Suriana Welfare Society Malaysia, which is helping the family raise the funds.
A long search for answers
Wei Yang’s parents first became concerned when he was about a year old. He could neither sit up nor roll over as expected, but doctors could not explain why.
With financial help from a relative, the family travelled to Australia and Singapore for further tests. They returned without answers.

At six, Wei Yang began biting his fingers and lips. Doctors at Universiti Malaya Medical Centre suspected a rare disease and ordered genetic testing. The diagnosis finally came when he was about eight.
His parents had spent years searching for an explanation and trying different treatments in the hope of helping him.
Today, the second of three brothers cannot stand or walk independently. He needs help with daily routines and constant supervision because he may injure himself without warning.
His parents have adapted their home and daily lives around his needs. But as his symptoms worsen, keeping him safe has become more physically demanding.
When medication is no longer enough
Wei Yang’s self-biting has become more frequent and forceful, sometimes requiring medical treatment.
Doctors have increased his medication to the maximum dosage, yet it has failed to control the urges.
The drugs also leave him drowsy, adding to the burden of his care.
When severe spasms strike, one parent may not be enough to hold him safely. Both must intervene. They also watch over him at night, knowing an episode can leave him crying and exhausted.
Doctors have recommended DBS, which involves implanting electrodes to help regulate abnormal brain activity. The family was told about the procedure years ago but could not afford it.
With the self-injury worsening despite medication, doctors now believe it should be pursued as soon as possible.
Further delay could leave Wei Yang at greater risk of injury, while higher medication doses could cause more drowsiness, according to the medical advice provided to the family.
An urgent brain MRI and the operation can be scheduled once the necessary funds are available.
The estimated cost has risen from RM250,000 to between RM280,000 and RM300,000, including additional needs such as medication and a special wheelchair.
With RM40,000 collected, the family faces a shortfall of RM240,000 to RM260,000, depending on the final cost.
The boy beyond the illness
Despite the demands of his condition, Wei Yang has his own interests and ways of connecting with those around him.
He recognises familiar voices, operates his iPad himself and enjoys watching television. He also plays with toys that help strengthen his hand muscles. When someone offers him a hand, he takes it.
His mother recalls that when she cries, he asks if she is upset because of him. He also tells her he will try not to hurt himself.
For a mother, those words are especially painful. Her son wants to reassure her, yet the involuntary urges are beyond his control.
Both parents are getting older, and the physical demands of caring for him are becoming harder to manage. They also worry about who will look after him when they can no longer do so.
For now, their focus is on securing the treatment doctors believe could help.
The adapted chair remains a daily reminder of how far a father has gone to protect his son. But his ingenuity and the parents’ constant vigilance cannot replace the medical help Wei Yang needs.
They are appealing to Malaysians to help them raise the remaining funds.
Donations can be made to Suriana Welfare Society Malaysia, RHB account 262 689 0000 2614, using the reference 'KWY26'.
For more information, contact Rachel Ho at 012-211 4444 or Ivan Lee at 012-333 0022.
b147e1c72d173b4c: PUCHONG: Sebuah kerusi dibeli di IKEA yang diubah suai sendiri menjadi antara cara Kong Hean Fui melindungi anak lelakinya berusia 15 tahun daripada mencederakan diri akibat pergerakan di luar kawalan.

Dia mengubah suai kerusi itu dengan memasang tali pengikat bagi memastikan Kong Wei Yang selamat apabila pergerakan luar kawalan menguasai tubuhnya. Kekejangan itu kadangkala begitu kuat sehingga pengikat berkenaan perlu kerap dibaiki atau diganti.
Namun, kerusi itu tidak sentiasa mampu melindunginya.

Apabila kekejangan berlaku secara tiba-tiba, Wei Yang mungkin menghentak kakinya ke lantai atau menggigit jarinya begitu kuat sehingga ibu bapanya sukar melepaskan gigitan itu tanpa menyebabkan kecederaan lebih serius. Ada kalanya, kedua-duanya terpaksa menahannya bersama-sama.
Bagi Kong dan isterinya, Wong Yin Teng, menjaga anak mereka bermakna perlu sentiasa berwaspada siang dan malam.
Wei Yang menghidap sindrom Lesch-Nyhan, penyakit genetik yang jarang berlaku dan menyebabkan gangguan saraf, pergerakan otot di luar kawalan serta kecenderungan mencederakan diri secara kompulsif.

Kini, tabiat menggigit dirinya semakin sukar dikawal walaupun dengan ubat. Ibu bapanya berharap dia akhirnya dapat menjalani prosedur yang disyorkan doktor sejak beberapa tahun lalu, namun kosnya di luar kemampuan mereka.

Rayuan bantuan yang disiarkan FMT pada Julai berjaya mengumpul kira-kira RM40,000 sebelum sumbangan mula berkurangan. Keluarga itu kini memerlukan antara RM280,000 hingga RM300,000 untuk prosedur rangsangan otak dalam (DBS), yang bertujuan membantu mengawal gejalanya.
Wang yang dikumpul masih dipegang Suriana Welfare Society Malaysia, yang membantu keluarga itu mengumpul dana.
Bertahun-tahun mencari jawapan

Ibu bapa Wei Yang mula menyedari sesuatu yang tidak kena ketika dia berusia kira-kira setahun. Pada usia itu, dia masih tidak mampu duduk sendiri atau berguling seperti kanak-kanak lain, namun doktor tidak dapat menjelaskan puncanya.
Dengan bantuan kewangan seorang saudara, keluarga itu membawanya ke Australia dan Singapura untuk menjalani pemeriksaan lanjut. Namun, mereka pulang tanpa jawapan.

Ketika berusia enam tahun, Wei Yang mula menggigit jari dan bibirnya. Doktor di Pusat Perubatan Universiti Malaya mengesyaki dia menghidap penyakit jarang berlaku lalu menjalankan ujian genetik. Diagnosis akhirnya diperoleh ketika dia berusia kira-kira lapan tahun.
Ibu bapanya menghabiskan bertahun-tahun mencari punca keadaannya dan mencuba pelbagai rawatan dengan harapan dapat membantu anak mereka.

Kini, Wei Yang yang merupakan anak kedua daripada tiga beradik lelaki tidak mampu berdiri atau berjalan sendiri. Dia memerlukan bantuan untuk menjalani rutin harian serta pengawasan berterusan kerana boleh mencederakan diri pada bila-bila masa.

Ibu bapanya turut menyesuaikan rumah dan kehidupan harian mereka mengikut keperluannya. Namun, apabila gejalanya semakin teruk, usaha memastikan keselamatannya menjadi semakin mencabar dari segi fizikal.
Apabila ubat tidak lagi mencukupi
Tabiat Wei Yang menggigit dirinya kini menjadi lebih kerap dan kuat sehingga ada kalanya memerlukan rawatan perubatan.
Doktor sudah meningkatkan dos ubatnya ke tahap maksimum, namun ia masih gagal mengawal dorongan itu.
Ubat berkenaan turut menyebabkan dia mengantuk, sekali gus menambah cabaran dalam menguruskannya.

Apabila kekejangan teruk berlaku, seorang daripada ibu bapanya sahaja mungkin tidak mampu menahannya dengan selamat. Kedua-duanya terpaksa membantu. Mereka turut memantaunya pada waktu malam kerana episod sedemikian boleh menyebabkan Wei Yang menangis dan keletihan.

Doktor mengesyorkan prosedur DBS, yang melibatkan pemasangan elektrod untuk membantu mengawal aktiviti otak yang tidak normal. Keluarga itu sudah dimaklumkan mengenai prosedur tersebut beberapa tahun lalu, tetapi tidak mampu menanggung kosnya.
Memandangkan perbuatan mencederakan diri semakin teruk walaupun sudah mengambil ubat, doktor kini berpendapat prosedur itu perlu dilakukan secepat mungkin.

Berdasarkan nasihat perubatan yang diberikan kepada keluarga, kelewatan lanjut boleh meningkatkan risiko Wei Yang mengalami kecederaan, manakala dos ubat yang lebih tinggi boleh menyebabkan dia menjadi semakin mengantuk.
Imbasan MRI otak yang perlu dilakukan segera dan pembedahan boleh dijadualkan sebaik sahaja dana mencukupi.
Anggaran kos kini meningkat daripada RM250,000 kepada antara RM280,000 hingga RM300,000, termasuk keperluan tambahan seperti ubat-ubatan dan kerusi roda khas.
Dengan RM40,000 sudah dikumpul, keluarga itu masih kekurangan antara RM240,000 hingga RM260,000, bergantung kepada kos akhir rawatan.
Wei Yang di sebalik penyakitnya
Di sebalik segala cabaran yang dihadapinya, Wei Yang mempunyai minat tersendiri dan cara untuk berinteraksi dengan orang di sekelilingnya.

Dia mengenali suara yang biasa didengarnya, boleh menggunakan iPad sendiri dan gemar menonton televisyen. Dia juga bermain dengan alat permainan yang membantu menguatkan otot tangannya. Apabila seseorang menghulurkan tangan, dia akan menyambutnya.
Ibunya berkata apabila dia menangis, Wei Yang akan bertanya sama ada dia bersedih kerana dirinya. Dia juga memberitahu ibunya bahawa dia akan cuba untuk tidak mencederakan dirinya lagi.
Bagi seorang ibu, kata-kata itu amat menyentuh hati. Anaknya mahu menenangkan perasaannya, sedangkan dorongan luar kawalan itu bukan sesuatu yang mampu dikawal Wei Yang.

Kedua-dua ibu bapanya semakin berusia dan tuntutan fizikal untuk menjaganya juga menjadi semakin berat. Mereka turut bimbang siapa yang akan menjaga Wei Yang apabila suatu hari nanti mereka tidak lagi mampu berbuat demikian.
Buat masa ini, tumpuan mereka adalah mendapatkan rawatan yang dipercayai doktor mampu membantu anak mereka.

Kerusi yang diubah suai itu menjadi peringatan setiap hari tentang sejauh mana seorang bapa sanggup berusaha untuk melindungi anaknya. Namun, segala ikhtiarnya serta pengawasan berterusan ibu bapa tidak mampu menggantikan rawatan perubatan yang diperlukan Wei Yang.
Keluarga itu merayu bantuan rakyat Malaysia bagi mengumpul baki dana rawatan.
Sumbangan boleh disalurkan kepada Suriana Welfare Society Malaysia, akaun RHB 262 689 0000 2614, dengan menggunakan rujukan ‘KWY26’.
Untuk maklumat lanjut, hubungi Rachel Ho di 012-211 4444 atau Ivan Lee di 012-333 0022.

7fb25f7f1ccd93ee: KUALA LUMPUR: Pas' decision to prioritise Umno and Barisan Nasional in negotiations for the next general election signals a willingness to explore closer cooperation, but does not yet indicate a new electoral alliance is taking shape, says a political analyst.

Universiti Malaya political analyst Dr Tawfik Yaakub said the decision by Pas' Syura Council gave the party's central leadership room to pursue talks with Umno and BN while potentially strengthening its bargaining position with other political parties.
"This is a meaningful signal of strategic intent, but it is not yet evidence of a settled electoral realignment.
"Whether it represents a genuine shift will depend on whether both sides move from statements to concrete discussions on seats, leadership and a shared policy platform," he said.
Yesterday, Pas spiritual leader Datuk Hashim Jasin said the party would prioritise Umno and BN over other political parties in negotiations for the next general election.
Hashim said the decision was made at a recent Syura Council meeting he chaired, which mandated the party's central leadership to negotiate with any party, with Umno given priority.
He said the council recognised that bringing Pas and Umno together would not be easy and that the opportunity should be fully utilised.
Hashim added that Pas was more comfortable cooperating with Umno than with other parties, noting that the people wanted unity between the two Malay-Muslim parties.
He also said the unity must be built on the interests of the Malays and Islam rather than political considerations.

Asked whether the decision could create unease within Perikatan Nasional, Tawfik said it could, particularly if Umno was treated as Pas's preferred partner without clear consultation with other component parties.
"The challenge for Pas will be to pursue talks with Umno without weakening trust among its existing partners," he said.
On the possibility of a renewed Pas-Umno arrangement, Tawfik said such cooperation was possible but would require substantial compromises to remain viable.

"Both parties would need to reach agreement on seat allocation, candidate selection, leadership arrangements and the terms of any post-election cooperation, while addressing longstanding issues of trust and political rivalry.
"They would also need to demonstrate that the partnership was based on more than a temporary electoral bargain," he said.

Tawfik said cooperation between the two parties could reduce competition for Malay-Muslim votes in certain constituencies, but would not automatically consolidate those voters behind a single alliance.
"Supporters may have different priorities and may not accept every compromise made by their party leadership," he said.
He added that the arrangement could also create divisions within the parties and raise questions among BN's non-Malay partners and voters about the coalition's political direction.

On which party stood to gain more from the proposed cooperation, Tawfik said Pas could gain more immediate political leverage by using the prospect of an alliance to strengthen its negotiating position.
Umno, meanwhile, could benefit from access to Pas's support base and an opportunity to rebuild its political relevance, although it risked being perceived as the junior partner.
"The eventual balance of gains will depend on the seat-sharing formula, the leadership arrangement and each party's ability to retain its own identity and supporters," he said.

3ad00f13eed60bce: THE recent Musicians for Malaysia charity concert, themed Rocking For A Cause, brought together some of the country's best-known bands that rose to fame across the club and restaurant circuits over the last six decades.
The annual fundraiser, which channels its proceeds towards musicians in need, took place at Kelab Golf Negara Subang (KGNS) in Petaling Jaya and featured three hours of non-stop live music.
A total of 21 musicians — mostly veterans — received honorary plaques for their contributions to the music industry.

The concert was held alongside a dinner attended by 560 guests from across the Klang Valley, Melaka, Johor, and Penang, with some travelling from as far as the United States, New Zealand, and Australia.
Musicians for Malaysia (MfM) honorary secretary Latifah Abdullah shared that the event successfully raised RM85,500.
The evening paid special tribute to active veteran performers aged 75 and above. Ten musicians suffering from illnesses and in need of medical assistance will benefit directly from the proceeds.

Among the 21 honoured musicians were Alfred Ho, Tinoy Soliano, Radha Krishnan, Frankie Tan, Ruzlan Omar, Rusli Musif (Olie of Heavy Machine), Royston Sta Maria, Kenny Tay, and MfM president Francis Danker.

Latifah said: "This is the fourth edition of our MfM showcase and it once again celebrates musicians whose careers have helped shape the country's musical landscape. Each of the recipients was given a plaque in recognition of their contribution to the development of the industry."
She added: "We want to recognise them because no one has ever given them such recognition, despite their long involvement in the music industry and the fact that they continue to work to this day."
VETERANS
The veteran bands entertaining guests throughout the show included Electric Orgasm, Goblokes, Heavy Machine, Lighthouse featuring Vijay David, Os Pombos, The Polymaths, and The Studio 10 Experience.
Among the soloists, Australian-based singer-songwriter Royston (Roy) Sta Maria and evergreen songstress Datuk Francissca Peter (Fran) were easily the biggest names.
Anyone who grew up in the 1980s would instantly remember them as the Malaysian "Donny & Marie Osmond" of that era: Roy & Fran.

While some die-hard fans hoped the iconic duet partners would take to the stage together for classic hits like 'Siapa Dia Sebelum Daku', they focused instead on their respective solo smash hits from the 1980s.

Fran opened her set with several trademark songs, starting with 'Sekadar Di Pinggiran' — the song that won the inaugural Anugerah Juara Lagu in 1986. The crowd sang and waved along as Fran sportingly pointed her microphone towards the tables.
Her upbeat hit 'Oo La La Tropika' was another crowd favourite, recalling her heyday, performed in signature colourful outfits and iconic 1980s "high hair".

"We're here to have a great time going down memory lane and reliving those magical moments of Malaysian music. I'm truly happy to reunite with many old friends, and I promise I'll be back as long as I can," said Fran, who was accompanied by her mother, Alice Peters.
Fran, who has released 10 solo albums, was the first Malaysian artiste to win Best Song at the Asean Song Festival in Kuala Lumpur in 1987.

Her last major concert was held at Istana Budaya in 2011 to mark her 33rd year in the music industry — a sold-out, three-night event accompanied by a 33-piece orchestra, with Roy as premier guest star.
ANTICIPATED REUNION
When Roy took to the stage, he delivered his legendary composition 'Mulanya Di Sini' alongside Freedom, the band that made it famous.

It was a highly anticipated reunion for the popular 1980s group. Founder member Shuib paid tribute to Roy, the band, and their late original lead singer, Seha Abu Bakar, while archival images of the original line-up flashed across the big screen.
Roy, 74, who now lives in Perth, Australia, noted that the song has become an enduring national anthem.
"My composition has travelled across generations, been performed by countless musicians and four decades after it was first penned, it continues to find its place in popular culture," he said.
'Mulanya Di Sini' achieved its breakthrough when it represented Malaysia at the third Asean Song Festival in 1986, finishing second before appearing on Freedom's 1987 debut album.
Roy added that the track has featured in countless television commercials over the last 40 years.
The duo released two albums around the turn of the decade before going their separate ways in 1984, though they still catch up in Kuala Lumpur every few years.
IMPERSONATIONS & ENTERTAINMENT
The third major star was Datuk Leonard Tan, fondly known as the "Singer with a Thousand Voices" and the "King of Jingles".
The singer, actor, and comedian is celebrated for his spot-on impersonations of icons like Louis Armstrong, the Bee Gees and Tan Sri P. Ramlee.

Looking sharp in a Nehru jacket, Tan belted out classics including Neil Diamond's 'Sweet Caroline', Lionel Richie's 'Stuck On You', Whitney Houston's 'Greatest Love Of All', and Al Jarreau's 'Spain', stepping off stage to let delighted diners finish his lyrics.
Tan, who sings seamlessly in English, Malay, and Chinese, said: "I believe that as a Malaysian, mastering our country's languages is a goal worth striving for."

Emcee Radha (aka The Black Stallion), 75, kept the event lively. The veteran singer and presenter earned his racehorse nickname due to his knack for mimicking fast-talking racing commentators and galloping hooves.
"More importantly, it reflects my high-energy stage presence — whether I'm singing, performing comedy, presenting radio shows, or hosting live events," he said to warm applause.
Rounding off the evening, veteran group Electric Orgasm marked its 50th anniversary, taking guests back in time with covers of local and Western classics.
The band's star line-up included Radha, Roy, Fauzi Marzuki, and Nasser Abu Kassim — all of whom went on to forge successful solo careers.

d25a41d84637b5f6: The recent announcement that Budget 2027 will provide funding for public transport is a good step forward. Hopefully, more funding will go beyond the Klang Valley, with Johor Bahru and other state capitals receiving their allocations by June next year.

Between now and June, there is still time to undertake a proper demand assessment, a fundamental component of transport planning. Without a proper understanding of travel patterns, passenger volumes, origins and destinations, even expensive infrastructure projects can fail to deliver their intended benefits.

Unfortunately, transport planning in Malaysia has so far been biased towards road transport, driven mainly by federal government decisions and funding, and often mired in political considerations rather than based on a comprehensive assessment of actual needs and demand.
The Johor Bahru-Singapore corridor is a classic example. For decades, demand for travel between the two cities has exceeded the capacity of the transport infrastructure and services available.

Hundreds of thousands of people cross the border daily for work, business, education and other activities. The pressure on the Causeway is known and well documented. Sketchy improvements in the form of costly new technology — such as QR codes for documentation processing — have not eased daily congestion, especially when systems break down as they often do.

Despite this longstanding demand, the question remains: have we made the best use of our existing infrastructure, especially the rail facilities, before committing ourselves to more expensive solutions?
The Tebrau shuttle service: a missed opportunity?

Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad’s (KTMB) rail lines across the causeway may be old tech by today's standard, but the Tebrau shuttle service between Johor Bahru and Woodlands has demonstrated the value of rail travel across the border. The actual train journey takes only five minutes, making it considerably faster than travelling by road during peak periods.
However, the service has historically been constrained by limited seating capacity and ticket availability, and the difficulty of accommodating the large number of commuters who wish to use it.
Between 5am and 7.30am, a train departs every 30 minutes. After 7.30am, passengers may face waits of up to 1½ hours for the next departure.

This raises an important question. If demand for cross-border travel is so substantial, why has the existing railway service not been upgraded more aggressively to accommodate the high passenger volume?

Why are the intervals between trains so long, resulting in lengthy waits? Why must every passenger buying a ticket be assigned a seat when the journey takes only five minutes each way, when some may be willing to stand?
The answer cannot simply be that its replacement — a new, modern and technologically more advanced railway system — is already under construction.

What if we first examined the operational and regulatory constraints, existing railway capacity, options for increasing service frequency, border immigration arrangements and the feasibility of expanding operations?
Railway infrastructure is expensive to build. Where tracks and stations already exist, improving the utilisation of those assets should be an obvious starting point, and could cost much less.
The RTS Link: necessary, but an incomplete solution

It has been said that the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link will transform cross-border commuting. With a journey time of about six minutes between Bukit Chagar and Woodlands North and planned intervals of around 10 minutes or less, the RTS Link will offer commuters an alternative to road travel across the Causeway.

Its importance should not be underestimated. However, the RTS should not be regarded as a stand-alone or final solution to Johor Bahru's transport problems. Its success will depend heavily on how passengers travel to and from Bukit Chagar station.

If commuters must depend on buses, private cars, taxis or ride-hailing services to reach the station, congestion could simply shift from the Causeway to the roads surrounding Bukit Chagar. The station's passenger-handling capacity, pedestrian access, bus connectivity, drop-off facilities and integration with other public transport services will need to be planned and integrated seamlessly.

More importantly, it has to be recognised that the RTS primarily serves a specific cross-border corridor link. It does not automatically solve the wider mobility problems faced by residents travelling between different parts of Johor Bahru, Permas Jaya, Iskandar Puteri and the surrounding Johor Bahru conurbations.
We must therefore distinguish between a project that improves a cross-border link and a transport system that improves mobility throughout the city. They are not the same thing.
How does KTMB fit into the bigger picture?

KTMB has more than one line in Johor Bahru. Apart from the new double-track intercity line linking central Johor Bahru with Gemas and Kuala Lumpur, there is also a branch line from Kempas Baru, north of Johor Bahru, to Pasir Gudang in the east.

Another branch line just south of Senai forms a triangular route with the main line, connecting Senai to Iskandar Puteri and Tanjung Pelepas in western Johor. It is also possible for a train from Tanjung Pelepas to travel to Senai, Sedenak, Kluang, Gemas and all the way to Kuala Lumpur.
Using the same line, a train can also provide services from Tanjung Pelepas directly to Senai, using the Kempas Baru junction to get to Pasir Gudang or go directly south to Johor Bahru and Woodlands.

Unfortunately, such services (or a configuration of my imagined passenger services) are currently not available, even though the tracks there are all in good order and condition, and obviously underutilised, reportedly because there are no suitable coaches and locomotives to run such services.

This is one of my concerns: has sufficient attention been given to the future role of KTMB’s existing railway infrastructure network. i.e. whether it can be turned into an effective passenger commuter service? Reports suggest that funding has instead been directed toward an elevated autonomous rapid transit system.

The Tebrau shuttle service should not be abandoned once the RTS Link is up and running. Instead, it should be combined into the wider KTMB network mentioned above to serve different travel demands and purposes.

Like the RTS Link, public transport in Johor Bahru should not be planned piecemeal or in isolation from other services. Integrated planning and demand management must be comprehensive, free from political influence, and considered within the broader framework of transport planning for greater Johor Bahru.
There is an opportunity to extend the Tebrau shuttle service to Senai town and eventually to Senai International Airport. From there, the service could branch towards Pasir Gudang via Kempas Baru.

While the RTS will provide a higher‑capacity link to Woodlands North, the KTMB network could serve as a feeder line, collecting passengers along existing routes that are not easily reached by other transport modes.
There is nothing wrong with providing two rail network options into Woodlands from more than one location in Johor Bahru.

The challenge is determining how these services can complement one another rather than leave gaps in growing transport demand. Johor Bahru’s public transport network should follow future demand, not politics.

b4547c06c02d691d: PETALING JAYA: For decades, the leatherback turtle was one of Terengganu’s most famous visitors, drawing crowds to Rantau Abang to watch the world’s largest sea turtle crawl ashore under cover of darkness.
Then the visits dwindled, with the last recorded nesting in the state taking place in 2017.
That is why the events of the past six weeks have caused such excitement. Since Sept 1, five leatherback nesting events have been recorded along the Terengganu coast, producing a total of 313 eggs.
The latest occurred at Pantai Rantau Abang on Oct 10, when a turtle came ashore at about 3am, laid its eggs at 4.30am and returned to the sea around 5.45am.
A total of 48 eggs were collected and transferred to a controlled hatchery at the Rantau Abang Turtle Conservation and Information Centre (TCIC).
“This brings the total number of leatherback turtle eggs recorded from the five landings to 313,” fisheries department director-general Adnan Hussain said in a statement.

The first nesting was recorded on Sept 1 at Pantai Pasir Putih in Marang, where 44 eggs were collected. That was followed by 81 eggs at Pantai Rantau Abang on Sept 13, 70 at Pantai Kuala Abang on Sept 22, and another 70 at Pantai Jambu Bongkok on Oct 1.
After the first landing, state fisheries department director Pang Nyukang described the turtle’s return as a hopeful sign after a nine-year absence.
“The rediscovery of the leatherback turtle brings new hope that future generations will be able to witness the existence of this ancient creature,” he said.

The department cautioned, however, that the nesting events do not necessarily represent five different turtles. Leatherbacks can return several times during the same nesting season, and officials have said the same individual may have been responsible for more than one of the recent landings.

The next question is whether the eggs will hatch successfully. Leatherback eggs typically incubate for around 55 to 70 days depending on sand temperature and nest conditions, with eggs from the first nest expected to hatch between Oct 26 and Nov 10.
All of the eggs have been transferred to controlled hatchery conditions, where the nests are monitored and managed to improve their chances of survival.
Adnan said the TCIC would continue regular monitoring until hatching was complete, while stressing the importance of scientific monitoring, nest management, enforcement and community participation.

Success is far from guaranteed. According to the fisheries department, the last two leatherback nesting events recorded in Terengganu in 2017 produced 124 eggs, but they are believed to have failed to hatch because they were unfertilised.

The return carries particular emotional weight in Rantau Abang, once internationally renowned for its leatherbacks. As nesting numbers collapsed over the decades, so too did much of the turtle-watching tourism that had grown around their visits.

The turtles’ return has also brought renewed attention to how people behave around nesting sites. Authorities have urged the public not to touch turtles, disturb nests or take eggs, while tourism operators and residents have been asked to reduce lighting along the coastline during nesting season.
Pang summed up the conservation message after the first turtle returned in September: “Let’s pray that all the turtle eggs can hatch and the baby turtles can swim back to the ocean safely.”

For now, that is exactly what conservationists and turtle lovers are waiting for. After nearly a decade without a recorded nesting, Terengganu has leatherback eggs beneath the sand again - and the coming weeks will reveal whether a new generation is ready to emerge.
6e96ba8bd8685661: Pengumuman baru-baru ini bahawa Belanjawan 2027 akan menyediakan peruntukan untuk pengangkutan awam adalah satu langkah yang baik.
Diharapkan lebih banyak peruntukan akan disalurkan ke luar Lembah Klang, termasuk kepada Johor Bahru dan ibu negeri lain menjelang Jun tahun depan.
Antara sekarang hingga Jun, masih ada masa untuk menjalankan penilaian menyeluruh terhadap permintaan pengguna, yang merupakan asas penting dalam perancangan pengangkutan.

Tanpa pemahaman yang jelas mengenai corak perjalanan, jumlah penumpang serta lokasi asal dan destinasi mereka, projek infrastruktur yang mahal sekalipun mungkin gagal memberikan manfaat seperti diharapkan.
Malangnya, perancangan pengangkutan di Malaysia selama ini lebih tertumpu kepada pengangkutan jalan raya, didorong terutamanya oleh keputusan dan pembiayaan kerajaan persekutuan.
Dalam banyak keadaan, pertimbangan politik turut mempengaruhi keputusan, berbanding penilaian menyeluruh terhadap keperluan dan permintaan sebenar.
Koridor Johor Bahru-Singapura adalah contoh yang jelas.
Sejak berdekad-dekad lalu, permintaan perjalanan antara kedua-dua bandar itu melebihi kapasiti infrastruktur dan perkhidmatan pengangkutan yang tersedia.
Ratusan ribu orang menyeberangi sempadan setiap hari untuk bekerja, berniaga, belajar dan melakukan pelbagai urusan lain.
Tekanan terhadap Tambak Johor sudah diketahui dan didokumentasikan dengan baik.

Namun, penambahbaikan secara kecil-kecilan menggunakan teknologi baharu yang mahal, seperti kod QR untuk pemprosesan dokumen, masih gagal mengurangkan kesesakan harian, terutama apabila sistem mengalami gangguan seperti yang kerap berlaku.

Walaupun permintaan ini sudah berlarutan begitu lama, persoalannya ialah sama ada kita benar-benar memanfaatkan infrastruktur sedia ada, khususnya kemudahan rel, sebelum beralih kepada penyelesaian yang lebih mahal.
Perkhidmatan Shuttle Tebrau: peluang yang terlepas?
Landasan Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) merentasi Tambak Johor mungkin dianggap teknologi lama mengikut piawaian hari ini.
Namun, perkhidmatan Shuttle Tebrau antara Johor Bahru dan Woodlands membuktikan nilai pengangkutan rel bagi perjalanan rentas sempadan.
Perjalanan sebenar dengan kereta api hanya mengambil masa kira-kira lima minit, jauh lebih pantas berbanding perjalanan jalan raya ketika waktu puncak.
Bagaimanapun, perkhidmatan itu sejak sekian lama berdepan kekangan kapasiti tempat duduk dan ketersediaan tiket, selain tidak mampu menampung jumlah besar penumpang yang mahu menggunakannya.
Antara 5 pagi hingga 7.30 pagi, kereta api bergerak setiap 30 minit.
Selepas 7.30 pagi, penumpang mungkin perlu menunggu sehingga satu setengah jam untuk perjalanan berikutnya.
Ini menimbulkan persoalan penting.
Jika permintaan perjalanan rentas sempadan begitu tinggi, mengapa perkhidmatan rel sedia ada tidak dinaik taraf dengan lebih agresif bagi menampung jumlah penumpang yang besar?
Mengapa jarak masa antara perjalanan terlalu panjang sehingga menyebabkan penumpang terpaksa menunggu lama?
Mengapa pula setiap penumpang yang membeli tiket perlu diberikan tempat duduk sedangkan perjalanan hanya mengambil masa lima minit sehala, sedangkan mungkin ada yang sanggup berdiri?
Jawapannya tidak sepatutnya sekadar kerana penggantinya, iaitu sistem rel baharu yang lebih moden dan berteknologi tinggi, sedang dibina.

Bagaimana jika kita terlebih dahulu meneliti kekangan operasi dan kawal selia, kapasiti rel sedia ada, pilihan meningkatkan kekerapan perjalanan, urusan imigresen di sempadan serta kemungkinan memperluaskan operasi?
Pembinaan infrastruktur rel memerlukan kos yang tinggi.
Jika landasan dan stesen sudah tersedia, usaha memaksimumkan penggunaannya sepatutnya menjadi titik permulaan kerana kosnya mungkin jauh lebih rendah.
RTS Link perlu, tetapi bukan penyelesaian lengkap
Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link dikatakan akan mengubah perjalanan ulang-alik rentas sempadan.

Dengan masa perjalanan kira-kira enam minit antara Bukit Chagar dan Woodlands North serta kekerapan dirancang sekitar 10 minit atau kurang, RTS Link akan memberikan alternatif kepada pengguna selain perjalanan melalui jalan raya di Tambak Johor.
Kepentingannya tidak harus dipandang ringan.
Namun, RTS tidak wajar dianggap sebagai penyelesaian tunggal atau penyelesaian muktamad kepada masalah pengangkutan Johor Bahru.
Kejayaannya banyak bergantung kepada bagaimana penumpang pergi ke dan meninggalkan stesen Bukit Chagar.

Jika pengguna masih perlu bergantung kepada bas, kereta persendirian, teksi atau perkhidmatan e-hailing untuk ke stesen, kesesakan mungkin hanya berpindah dari Tambak Johor ke jalan raya di sekitar Bukit Chagar.

Kapasiti stesen mengendalikan penumpang, akses pejalan kaki, hubungan dengan perkhidmatan bas, kemudahan menurunkan penumpang serta integrasi dengan pengangkutan awam lain perlu dirancang dengan baik dan diselaraskan secara menyeluruh.
Lebih penting, kita perlu memahami bahawa RTS pada asasnya berfungsi untuk satu koridor rentas sempadan tertentu.

Ia tidak secara automatik menyelesaikan masalah pergerakan lebih luas yang dihadapi penduduk yang berulang-alik antara kawasan berbeza di Johor Bahru, Permas Jaya, Iskandar Puteri dan kawasan sekitar konurbasi Johor Bahru.
Kita perlu membezakan antara projek yang memperbaiki hubungan rentas sempadan dengan sistem pengangkutan yang meningkatkan pergerakan di seluruh bandar.
Kedua-duanya bukan perkara yang sama.
Di mana kedudukan KTMB dalam perancangan lebih besar?
KTMB mempunyai lebih daripada satu landasan di Johor Bahru.

Selain landasan berkembar antara bandar yang menghubungkan pusat Johor Bahru dengan Gemas dan Kuala Lumpur, terdapat juga landasan cabang dari Kempas Baru di utara Johor Bahru ke Pasir Gudang di timur.
Satu lagi landasan cabang di selatan Senai membentuk laluan berbentuk segi tiga bersama landasan utama, menghubungkan Senai dengan Iskandar Puteri dan Tanjung Pelepas di barat Johor.
Kereta api dari Tanjung Pelepas juga boleh bergerak ke Senai, Sedenak, Kluang, Gemas hingga ke Kuala Lumpur.

Menggunakan landasan sama, perkhidmatan kereta api juga boleh disediakan dari Tanjung Pelepas terus ke Senai, kemudian melalui persimpangan Kempas Baru ke Pasir Gudang, atau terus ke selatan menuju Johor Bahru dan Woodlands.
Malangnya, perkhidmatan sedemikian, atau apa-apa susunan perkhidmatan penumpang seperti yang saya bayangkan, belum tersedia ketika ini.
Ini walaupun landasan yang ada berada dalam keadaan baik dan jelas tidak digunakan sepenuhnya, dipercayai kerana tiada koc dan lokomotif yang sesuai untuk mengendalikan perkhidmatan sedemikian.
Inilah antara kebimbangan saya.
Adakah perhatian yang mencukupi sudah diberikan kepada peranan masa depan rangkaian rel KTMB sedia ada, termasuk kemungkinan menjadikannya perkhidmatan komuter penumpang yang berkesan?
Laporan menunjukkan pembiayaan sebaliknya disalurkan kepada sistem transit aliran autonomi bertingkat.
Perkhidmatan Shuttle Tebrau tidak sepatutnya dihentikan apabila RTS Link mula beroperasi.
Sebaliknya, ia wajar digabungkan dengan rangkaian KTMB yang lebih luas seperti dinyatakan tadi bagi memenuhi keperluan dan corak perjalanan yang berbeza.
Seperti RTS Link, pengangkutan awam di Johor Bahru tidak boleh dirancang secara berasingan atau sedikit demi sedikit tanpa mengambil kira perkhidmatan lain.

Perancangan bersepadu dan pengurusan permintaan perlu dibuat secara menyeluruh, bebas daripada pengaruh politik dan dilihat dalam kerangka lebih besar perancangan pengangkutan bagi seluruh kawasan Johor Bahru.
Terdapat juga peluang untuk melanjutkan perkhidmatan Shuttle Tebrau ke bandar Senai dan akhirnya ke Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Senai.
Dari situ, perkhidmatan boleh bercabang ke Pasir Gudang melalui Kempas Baru.

Walaupun RTS akan menyediakan hubungan berkapasiti lebih tinggi ke Woodlands North, rangkaian KTMB pula boleh berfungsi sebagai laluan pengantara dengan mengumpulkan penumpang di sepanjang laluan sedia ada yang sukar dicapai melalui mod pengangkutan lain.
Tiada salahnya menyediakan dua pilihan rangkaian rel menuju ke Woodlands dari lokasi berbeza di Johor Bahru.
Cabaran sebenar ialah menentukan bagaimana perkhidmatan itu boleh saling melengkapi, bukannya membiarkan jurang dalam memenuhi permintaan pengangkutan yang semakin meningkat.
Rangkaian pengangkutan awam Johor Bahru seharusnya dirancang berdasarkan permintaan masa depan, bukan kepentingan politik.

ed4d0c18c79f4309: SEOUL: North Korea has tested a "new-type" precision-guided torpedo system that uses artificial intelligence for target detection and guidance, state news agency KCNA reported early Saturday.
The underwater test-fire of the "super-speed" Zam-2.0 system took place on Thursday "to confirm the successful technical updating" of the weapon, the Korean Central News Agency said.
"AI technology was applied to the target detection and the guidance function of the new-type super-speed precisely guided torpedo," KCNA said.
Earlier this month, North Korea announced that it had proceeded with the AI-assisted launch of an intermediate-range hypersonic missile.
In September, the country's leader Kim Jong Un emphasised the need to raise "the level of artificial intelligence" in the country's weapons systems.
Analysts have said North Korea could be rapidly advancing its missile technology with Russian military support in exchange for sending troops to support its war against Ukraine.
bfddf37aaf0fa529: NAIROBI: Kenya has recorded its third case of Ebola, a close relative of the country's first two Ebola cases, the health ministry said on Friday.
The country had not reported a single case of the contagious virus until last week, after a Kenyan man who had been living in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) died after returning to Kenya.
Just over a week later a second man, a relative of the first, also tested positive for the virus while in quarantine.
The DRC declared its 17th Ebola outbreak in May. The deadly disease has killed more than 15,000 people in Africa over the past 50 years.
The 65-year-old woman was a "primary contact and a close relative of the first and second cases", the ministry said in a statement, adding that she had been in quarantine since October 6.
After developing symptoms, including "fever, sore throat and malaise", she was isolated and tested positive for the virus.
The ministry emphasised that the risk to the public "remains low" and there was "no evidence of community transmission."
It said of 130 contacts, 127 had been traced and were in quarantine, with efforts "ongoing to trace and quarantine the three remaining contacts."
On Wednesday, the ministry confirmed its second case, a 39-year-old relative of the first victim, stating he was in isolation and there was "no evidence" of any large-scale transmission of the virus.
The country has never previously reported a case.
Neighbouring Uganda recorded 20 people infected, almost all of whom had travelled from the neighbouring DRC, and two deaths, before being declared Ebola-free in August.
Kenya's first victim was a national, who has not been named but was referred to as a 40-year-old businessman.
He fell ill around a month ago and had been treated in the DRC, before travelling overland to the Ugandan capital, Kampala, and flying into Nairobi on October 3.
He was hospitalised in Nairobi but died on October 5, according to Health Minister Aden Duale.

According to Congolese health authorities, the outbreak has infected 9,066 people so far and caused 4,381 deaths since the emergence in the DRC of the Bundibugyo strain of the Ebola virus, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment.
812fc4c388e33bfb: MOSCOW: Ukrainian forces controlled only a small part of the eastern Donetsk region and its capture was among Russia's "main objectives", president Vladimir Putin told military leaders in remarks made public Friday.
Putin said Russian forces were waging an offensive across the "entire front line", and described his army's progress as "positive".
The Russian leader's comments came as the Ukraine war ground through its fifth year, with both sides struggling to make breakthroughs and US-led peace talks deadlocked over the issue of territory.
Russia has long pushed for full control of the Donetsk region, which it claims as its own, and has threatened to take it by force if Ukraine does not cede it through negotiations.
Ukraine, which has launched its own offensive in the Donetsk region, has called Moscow's demand a capitulation that would leave it vulnerable to a future Russian attack.
"On the whole I see a positive trend in the operations of the troop groupings," Putin told military leaders in a video published on the Kremlin website.
"Undoubtedly, one of the main objectives remains the liberation of the Donetsk People's Republic," he added, using the Kremlin's name for the region.
Ukrainian troops made some gains against Russia in the Donetsk region in September, according to an AFP analysis of data from the Institute for the Study of War.
Widespread drone use at the front has made swift, large-scale troop movements almost impossible, preventing either side from gaining a clear advantage in the more than four-and-a-half-year war.

a499d5563f43ff7a: PETALING JAYA: Wawasan has the potential to soften PAS’s hardline image and help Perikatan Nasional win support from non-Malay voters as well as Malay fence-sitters, an analyst said.

Mazlan Ali of Universiti Teknologi Malaysia said Hamzah Zainudin’s party, which welcomes members from all races, could serve as a conduit for PAS to broaden its influence beyond its traditional strongholds.
“The existing perception is that PAS is a fairly conservative party, with influence largely limited to the traditional Malay states,” he told FMT.

He said PAS, through its cooperation with Bersatu, had previously enjoyed cross-ethnic support when Perikatan Nasional was led by former prime minister Muhyiddin Yassin, particularly outside the northern states of Perlis, Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu.
However, with PAS and Bersatu having severed ties, Mazlan said Wawasan could step into that role to attract voters who are typically beyond the Islamic party’s reach.
He said this could be achieved as Wawasan’s membership is open to Malaysians of all races and religions.
PAS severed political ties with Bersatu on June 8, although both parties remain in PN.
Five days later, Hamzah, the former Bersatu deputy president, launched Wawasan, which was later accepted into PN together with Pejuang, led by former Kedah menteri besar Mukhriz Mahathir.
Mazlan said cooperation with Wawasan would be easier for PAS, as the party is not competing to be the “big brother” or dominant force in an alliance.
However, he said the situation was different with Umno, which aspires to return as the main force given its history and governance record over more than 60 years.
“Umno is certainly the bigger party and the oldest in historical terms,” he said.
Syaza Shukri of International Islamic University Malaysia disagreed, saying Wawasan’s presence was unlikely to change voters’ perception of PAS as a hardline party.
She said PAS’s conservative image was not necessarily a liability, as it continues to resonate with the party’s core supporters and segments of the Malay electorate.
“Wawasan’s role is really to get non-Malay support.
“So it is not about making PAS less hardline, but making PN as a whole more acceptable to non-Malays,” she said.
However, Syaza said Wawasan cannot achieve this on its own, and that Umno's presence may be essential to reshape perceptions of the coalition.
Governing experience

Apart from efforts to attract voter support, Syaza said the presence of figures such as Hamzah and Saifuddin Abdullah, who have both served in Cabinet, could help PN counter perceptions that the coalition lacks governing experience.

She added that their experience in portfolios such as home and foreign affairs was crucial, as PAS is still perceived as lacking leaders capable of engaging in policy debates beyond race and religion.
“If they had that, I believe they would push for policy discussions.
“That is why they are pushing Dr Sam forward, but he alone is not enough,” she said, referring to PAS vice-president and Terengganu menteri besar, Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar.
Mazlan agreed that Hamzah and Saifuddin’s experience as ministers, as well as their national image, could give PN an advantage.
“In terms of experience, leaders like Hamzah are far more experienced than their PAS counterparts,” he said.
He said that experience could help PN broaden its political approach by giving greater attention to policy issues rather than focusing solely on religion and race.
Such an approach, he said, was vital in attracting moderate and progressive voters who want PN to present concrete policies and solutions to national challenges.
41d87dc9b102328e: PETALING JAYA: Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) berpotensi mengimbangi imej PAS yang dilihat berpendirian keras, sekali gus membantu Perikatan Nasional (PN) menarik sokongan pengundi bukan Melayu dan Melayu atas pagar, kata penganalisis.

Mazlan Ali daripada Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) berkata pendekatan inklusif Wawasan pimpinan Ketua Pembangkang Hamzah Zainudin, yang membuka keahlian kepada semua kaum, boleh membantu PAS memperluas pengaruhnya di luar kubu tradisional parti itu.
“Persepsi yang wujud ialah PAS sebuah parti agak konservatif, dengan pengaruh hanya sekitar negeri-negeri Melayu tradisional,” katanya kepada FMT.

Menurutnya, PAS sebelum ini mendapat manfaat daripada sokongan rentas kaum ketika PN dipimpin bekas perdana menteri Muhyiddin Yassin, khususnya di luar negeri-negeri SG4 menerusi kerjasama dengan Bersatu.

Namun, selepas PAS memutuskan hubungan politik dengan Bersatu, Mazlan berkata Wawasan berpotensi mengambil alih peranan itu terutama dalam usaha menarik sokongan pengundi yang sukar didekati parti Islam berkenaan.
Jelasnya, ia boleh dilakukan menerusi keterbukaan Wawasan membuka keahlian kepada semua kaum dan agama.
PAS memutuskan hubungan politik dengan Bersatu pada 8 Jun lalu, walaupun kedua-duanya masih kekal dalam PN.
Lima hari kemudiannya Hamzah, bekas timbalan presiden Bersatu melancarkan Wawasan yang diterima menyertai PN bersama Pejuang pimpinan bekas Mukhriz Mahathir.
Mazlan berkata kerjasama dengan Wawasan lebih mudah bagi PAS kerana parti itu tidak bersaing menjadi ‘abang long’ atau kuasa dominan dalam sesebuah pakatan.
Namun jelasnya keadaan itu berbeza buat PAS dengan Umno yang mungkin mahu menjadi kuasa utama memandangkan sejarah serta rekod sebagai kerajaan selama lebih 60 tahun.
"Sudah pasti Umno sebagai parti lebih besar dan paling lama dari segi sejarah," katanya.

Bagaimanapun, Syaza Shukri daripada Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Malaysia (UIAM) berpandangan kehadiran Wawasan tidak semestinya mengubah persepsi pengundi terhadap PAS sebagai parti berpendirian keras.
Katanya, imej konservatif itu juga tidak semestinya menjadi kelemahan kerana masih mendapat tempat dalam kalangan penyokong PAS dan sebahagian pengundi Melayu.
“Peranan Wawasan sebenarnya ialah mendapatkan sokongan bukan Melayu.
“Jadi ia bukan soal menjadikan PAS kurang berpendirian keras tetapi menjadikan PN secara keseluruhan lebih boleh diterima oleh bukan Melayu,” katanya.
Namun, Syaza berpendapat Wawasan sahaja tidak mencukupi untuk mengubah persepsi terhadap gabungan itu dan melihat Umno masih diperlukan bagi tujuan berkenaan.
Pengalaman mentadbir

Selain usaha menarik sokongan pengundi, Syaza berkata kehadiran tokoh seperti Hamzah dan Saifuddin Abdullah yang pernah menganggotai Kabinet boleh membantu PN menangkis dakwaan gabungan itu kekurangan pengalaman mentadbir.

Katanya, pengalaman tokoh itu yang memegang portolio seperti keselamatan dalam negeri dan diplomatik antarabangsa cukup penting kerana PAS dilihat masih kekurangan pemimpin yang mampu membawa perbincangan dasar melangkaui isu agama dan kaum.
“Jika ada saya percaya mereka akan mendorong perbincangan mengenai dasar.
“Sebab itu mereka menolak Dr Sam ke depan, tetapi beliau seorang sahaja tidak mencukupi,” katanya, merujuk kepada Menteri Besar Terengganu Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar yang juga naib presiden PAS.
Mazlan turut senada pengalaman Hamzah dan Saifuddin sebagai menteri serta mempunyai imej nasional boleh menjadi kelebihan kepada PN.
“Dari sudut pengalaman, pemimpin seperti Hamzah berada pada kedudukan jauh lebih berpengalaman berbanding pemimpin PAS,” katanya.
Menurutnya, pengalaman pemimpin berkenaan boleh membantu PN memperluas pendekatan politiknya dengan memberi lebih tumpuan kepada isu dasar, bukan sekadar agama dan kaum.
Pendekatan itu, katanya, penting untuk menarik sokongan pengundi sederhana dan progresif yang mahu melihat PN menawarkan dasar serta penyelesaian kepada isu negara.
b9867af14eac810d: PETALING JAYA: It's one of the less-obvious weaknesses in estate planning - a family can be asset-rich on paper and still face a cash-flow problem after a death.

Property, savings, investments and other assets may eventually pass to beneficiaries, but not necessarily immediately. Until the estate is administered and the necessary processes are completed, access to those assets can be delayed.
In Malaysia, an estimated RM90 billion in assets is said to be frozen in probate, while 46,707 cases remained unresolved as of Dec 31.
For families, the consequences are practical rather than abstract. Mortgage payments, school fees, medical bills and everyday household expenses continue even while an estate is still being settled.

This matters even more in a country where many households have limited financial buffers. Bank Negara’s Financial Capability and Inclusion 2024 survey of 3,587 Malaysians found that 61% would struggle to raise RM1,000 in an emergency, while 40% relied solely on their own savings or those of family members as a safety net.
Seen in that context, estate planning is not simply about transferring wealth - it is also about managing the period between death and access.
Where there's a will...

A will remains one of the most important estate-planning tools because it sets out how assets should be distributed and who should manage the estate. But it does not remove the need for administration.
In straightforward cases, the department of the director-general of lands and mines has four months from the date of a complete application where there are no disputes.
In practice, however, family disagreements, incomplete documentation, late claims and the complexity of an estate can extend the process.

This distinction is important: a will can provide clarity over who is entitled to what, but it does not necessarily provide immediate liquidity to the people left behind. For households where one person carries most of the financial burden, that delay can be particularly difficult.
What about a living trust?

A living trust addresses a different part of the problem. Under such an arrangement, selected assets are transferred to a trustee during the donor’s lifetime and managed according to the terms of a trust deed.
The trustee then administers those assets for the benefit of named beneficiaries.

Unlike assets that remain solely in the deceased’s estate, assets properly placed in a trust are held within a separate structure. Depending on how the trust is set up, this can make it possible to provide for beneficiaries without waiting for the wider estate-administration process to conclude.
That does not make a trust automatically “better” than a will. The two serve different functions and can complement each other.

A will deals with the distribution of an estate after death. A trust can be used to create more specific arrangements around timing, access and purpose - for example, regular payments for household expenses, education or medical needs.

For Muslim families, estate planning also has to take into account faraid and other shariah requirements, which means the structure chosen needs to sit within the relevant legal and religious framework.
The overlooked issue: liquidity

This is where estate planning becomes less about documents and more about household resilience. A person may leave behind a valuable property, investments and retirement savings, but those assets do not necessarily help a surviving spouse pay next month’s bills if they cannot be readily accessed.

One useful exercise is to estimate how much cash the household would need for several months if the main source of income suddenly disappeared. If monthly commitments are RM5,000, for instance, a six-month buffer would amount to RM30,000.
That money does not necessarily have to sit in cash, but there should be some thought given to which funds or assets could realistically be reached during the transition period.

The same principle applies when considering a trust. Before setting one up, families should be clear about its purpose, which assets should be placed into it, who the beneficiaries are, and under what circumstances distributions should be made.
The trustee’s responsibilities, charges, service terms and the provisions of the trust deed also deserve careful scrutiny.

Estate planning is often framed as the question of what happens to your money after you die. A better question may be what happens to the people who depend on that money in the weeks and months immediately afterwards.
After all, the real measure of an estate plan is not simply how much wealth is left behind, but how well that wealth can continue to support the family it was meant for.

84abaa8d1634a53a: BRASILIA: Deforestation of the Brazilian Amazon has fallen to its lowest level in nearly 40 years, according to figures released Friday, in welcome news for leftist incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva days before a presidential runoff.

Between August 2025 and July 2026, 3,335 square kilometers of forest were cleared, a decline of nearly 42% over the previous year and the lowest level since records began in 1988, official statistics showed.
"It's an absolutely stratospheric drop...it's like a dream," environment minister Joao Paulo Capobianco told a press conference in the capital Brasilia.
The data was also hailed by Lula, whom polls show running neck-and-neck with conservative senator Flavio Bolsonaro ahead of the Oct 25 runoff.

Lula, a veteran left-wing leader, returned to office promising to end unlawful forest clearance by ranchers and illegal miners, which had soared under his far-right predecessor Jair Bolsonaro, the father of Flavio.
"Our goal is to achieve zero illegal deforestation by 2030," he reiterated Friday on X, after the deforestation data was released.
Brazil is home to approximately 60% of the world's largest rainforest, which plays a crucial role in absorbing greenhouse gases responsible for global warming.
The official deforestation rate is measured using the "Prodes" satellite system, operated by the National Institute for Space Research.
Deforestation has been steadily decreasing in the Amazon since 2022, with a cumulative drop of 71.2% over the four years since Lula was elected.
The figures, which have been attributed to greater monitoring and stiffer penalties for illegal logging, mark a dramatic about-turn since Jair Bolsonaro's presidency, from 2019 to 2022.
The Amazon lost around 11,600 square kilometers of forest under his watch -- almost 60 percent more than in the previous four years, official figures show.
Flavio Bolsonaro has praised his father, who is serving a 27-year sentence for coup plotting, for having opposed what he calls a "radical environmental agenda."
At the same time he has proposed treating the environment as a "strategic asset" and pledged to end "illegal deforestation" by 2029.
There was also good news from the vast Cerrado savanna south of the Amazon, where deforestation fell to its lowest levels since records there began in 2001.
From August 2025 to July 2026, 5,517 square kilometers of native vegetation were destroyed, representing a reduction of almost 24% in a year.
Marcio Astrini, executive secretary of the Climate Observatory, a network of over 100 civil society groups, praised the figures as a "historic victory".
"This demonstrates that Brazil plays a leading role in protecting forests and that, with political will, it is possible to curb chainsaws and greenhouse gas emissions," he said in a statement.
9f2103358a034e33: BEND, United States: The "hero" who shot dead a teenage gunman after he had already killed three children and a teacher at an elementary school was named Friday, as the US entered a familiar – and likely fruitless – debate about gun control in the wake of the latest tragedy.

Kaylub Giamanco raced into Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Oregon, after the shooter, identified by local media as 16-year-old John J. Griffin II, blasted his way through locked doors and opened fire on youngsters.

Kyle Giamanco said 36-year-old Kaylub, who has two children at the school, was driving home for his lunch break on Thursday when he heard gunshots and saw Griffin going into the special education room of the school.
Kaylub Giamanco has a permit to carry a concealed weapon, his brother told NBC, adding that he was having difficulty processing events at the moment and feels guilty that he did not save more people.
A woman identified as his mother told the local Fox affiliate she was "very proud" and that her son was "an absolute hero" before she read a prepared statement.
"He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support," she said.
US President Donald Trump hailed Giamanco as a "great hero."
"As bad as it was, we had a great hero that went in and did the business," Trump told journalists. "It's a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it."

On Friday, the small city in the US northwest was struggling to come to terms with a tragedy that took the lives of children aged five, eight and 11, as well as a teacher, the latest victims of America's epidemic of gun violence that all-too-frequently afflicts the nation's schools.
Streets were quiet in an area known for its natural beauty, with hiking trails and ski pistes nearby that attract tens of thousands of visitors every year.
Kristen Vanetsky, 52, told AFP she was in shock over the shooting at her grandson's school.
"My grandson should be in his classroom, with all of his friends," she said.
"Everybody should be in there learning, having fun, looking forward to their weekend, and it's just vacant," she said. "There's nothing. Even the birds are not here."
GUN VIOLENCE
Even as the city tried to process the tragic events, the familiar contours of an argument that plays out after every school shooting in the US began to harden.
The politically powerful National Rifle Association (NRA) praised the then-unidentified bystander who stepped in to prevent even greater loss of life.
"Yesterday's terrible act of violence in Oregon serves as another reminder of the importance of a law-abiding armed citizenry," the NRA said in a post on X.
The man's actions "exemplify the heroism of everyday citizens who are prepared and ready to respond when innocent lives are on the line," it added.
The NRA has invested millions of dollars campaigning for gun rights and supporting politicians who block the limits on ownership that the vast majority of Americans support.
Gun control advocates again lamented the ready availability of weaponry in a country where the number of gun-related deaths far outpaces most of the developed world.
"America's gun violence crisis is killing our babies. Enough is enough," gun-control group GIFFORDS said on X.

More than 360 mass shootings have been recorded across the United States this year, according to the Gun Violence Archive, which defines them as incidents in which at least four people are shot, excluding the gunman.
LONG GUN
Griffin's neighbours told AFP they had seen his mother taken away from the house she shared with the suspect on Thursday afternoon in a police patrol car.
That woman, Shauntai May Nickerson, was seen on Friday smoking a cigarette on the porch outside of her apartment and crying.
"If I could have prevented this, I would have," a tearful Nickerson said, according to The New York Times.
